headline: Gulf oil shock, Israel's tight vote and rate-hike bets shaped the week
summary: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, a stalled U.S.-Iran standoff and a report that Washington is preparing post-midterm strikes kept Brent near US$115, feeding 3.1% Canadian inflation and a widely expected Bank of Canada hike today. Israel's election left Netanyahu's bloc ahead but short of a majority, B.C. elected a Conservative majority, Olivia Chow won a second term in Toronto as several GTA incumbents fell, and Ottawa and Washington revived talks on steel and auto tariffs.

top.headline: U.S. reportedly tells Gulf allies to brace for Iran strikes after midterms
top.what: Houthi barrages on Saudi Arabia and a report that the U.S. told Gulf allies to brace for post-midterm strikes kept Brent between about US$111 and US$117.
top.why: This is the single biggest driver of global energy prices this year.

top.headline: Bank of Canada decides today, with a hike to 2.50% widely expected
top.what: Gas-driven inflation of 3.1% has most economists expecting the Bank of Canada to raise its rate to 2.50% at 9:45 a.m. today.
top.why: A hike would raise costs for variable-rate mortgages and lines of credit.

top.headline: Israel's count leaves no bloc near the 61 seats needed
top.what: Exit polls showed no majority; with about 77% counted, Netanyahu's bloc leads 54 to 47 with Arab parties at 19, all short of 61.
top.why: The outcome shapes Israel's Iran policy and, through it, oil prices.

top.headline: U.S. envoy reportedly warns Canada could be blamed for midterm losses
top.what: Ottawa and Washington are working on easing steel and auto tariffs, but a deal before the midterms is uncertain and new 50% tariffs start Oct. 30.
top.why: Steel and auto tariffs hit thousands of Ontario manufacturing jobs.

top.headline: Chow re-elected; GTA voters oust several mayors
top.what: Olivia Chow won about 54% in Toronto, while incumbents fell in Mississauga, Hamilton, Oakville and Milton.
top.why: New councils will set GTA property taxes, housing and transit priorities for four years.

top.headline: Midterms six days out; forecasters tilt toward a Democratic House
top.what: About 21 million Americans have already voted and forecasters lean toward a Democratic House, with the election six days away.
top.why: The result decides how freely Trump can act on tariffs, the Iran war and spending for the final two years of his term.

top.headline: B.C. elects a Conservative majority
top.what: Lorne Doerkson's Conservatives won about 64 of 93 seats in unofficial results, ending nine years of NDP government; David Eby resigned as NDP leader.
top.why: A new B.C. government keen on LNG and scrapping the industrial carbon tax could reshape national energy and trade debates.

top.headline: Joly won't meet Stelco owner's CEO without a plan to restore jobs
top.what: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly gave Cleveland-Cliffs 15 days to honour its job commitments at Stelco, where about 200 workers have been laid off and up to 500 jobs are affected.
top.why: Steel jobs at Stelco's Hamilton and Lake Erie plants are a pillar of Ontario's manufacturing economy.
